page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.8xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-hypervised virtual instance configured with 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at up to 3.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI. The defining attribute of this instance is its massive memory density, supplying 1024.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, which equates to a high 32:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It also integrates 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, with no GPU hardware attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable mid-tier computational throughput paired with strong memory subsystem bandwidth. The system achieves a multi-core stress-ng rating of 30956.71 and a PassMark CPU score of 36913.69, falling solidly in the median 50% tier of comparable platforms. Uncached large-block read operations register 138.74 GB/sec while write operations achieve 62.28 GB/sec. Application benchmarks indicate high capability for caching and key-value transactions, reaching 31.04 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and a static web serving throughput of 33.26 GB/sec. Pure CPU inference on large 70B parameter language models exhibits weak-to-poor performance (2.49 tokens/sec generation), reflecting the limitation of executing large models without hardware accelerators.

From an infrastructure investment perspective, the x2iedn.8xlarge delivers high qualitative value for enterprise platforms whose footprints are constrained strictly by RAM rather than raw processing density. Consolidating large-scale working sets into 1 TB of RAM reduces horizontal node scaling requirements and inter-instance network overhead. Key architectural tradeoffs involve the reliance on DDR4 rather than DDR5 memory and a relatively modest 32 vCPUs, meaning compute-bound batch jobs will see diminishing returns. The instance is suited for in-memory databases like Redis and SAP HANA, real-time analytics engines, massive database caching tiers, and memory-bound transactional systems requiring high local NVMe scratch space.
